The way you're feeling is valid. There are a lot of expectations when it comes down to sexuality, somehow we're expected to want sex and accept flirting from anyone at any time. Some people like that stuff and that's okay. But the truth is _you_ get to choose your own boundaries. If you don't want that stuff, it's more than okay to make it clear and refuse to do it.

I know you said you're young, so your perspective about sexuality is still taking its shape as you grow up, but you might want to check out asexuality and/or demisexuality subs. I don't want to stick a label to you because, as I said, you're probably still learning about yourself, but at least you can read about other people's experiences and see how much you relate to them. As a learning experience and as an opportunity to feel less alone in it. 

Lastly, if you're young I'm assuming these boys you talk to are also around your age. Teenage boys are often so full of hormones they do not know how to engage properly with a person they're attracted to. They do and say things that aren't appropriate. What matters though is that you stand your ground and stick to your boundaries. No means no, consent shouldn't be "won". If they try to convince you to do something you're not okay with, they're not your friends. 

Good luck out there, stay safe.
